I bring strong skills in Python, web development, data analysis and love turning creative ideas into working prototypes under tight deadlines.We are building a collaborative, high-energy team focused on creating an innovative, impactful solution and having fun along the way I am currently looking for teammates with backgrounds in frontend/backend
summary: Mission Architect is a multiplayer 3D space mission design game for one to four players. Teams choose a destination such as Earth, the Moon, Mars or Venus, pick a rocket, and build a spacecraft in a live 3D builder. They then launch it in a 3D countdown and handle emergencies year by year. A score out of 100 and a leaderboard rank each mission. Players define a mission objective, choose instruments, a launcher and an orbit, and manage budget, mass, power, communications, data and lifetime on live gauges. Each player takes a role (Mission Lead, Spacecraft Engineer, Science Lead or Comms & Ops), so teams must discuss trade-offs. A launch simulation and scoring system reward good engineering. Real NASA solar-flare data from DONKI drives the emergencies, and the Astronomy Picture of the Day and Planetary Fact Sheet add real context. Real missions fail when one decision quietly breaks another part of the design. This game lets students and the public see those trade-offs first-hand, practise teamwork, and learn how space missions are planned, using real NASA data.
details: Mission Architect is a multiplayer 3D space mission design game where one to four players act as a mission team. After logging in with a team code, each player takes a role (Mission Lead, Spacecraft Engineer, Science Lead or Comms & Ops) and controls only that role's settings, so the team must discuss trade-offs. Players choose a destination such as Earth, the Moon, Mars or Venus, either from a card or by clicking a planet in an interactive 3D solar system, then pick a rocket, instruments and spacecraft settings while a 3D model rebuilds live and dial gauges track mass, power, data, lifetime and cost. A 3D launch with countdown, Max-Q and stage separation leads into a year-by-year mission where emergencies appear, some built from real NASA DONKI solar-flare data, and the result is a score out of 100 with achievements and a leaderboard. The game helps students and the public see how one decision affects every part of a mission and why teamwork matters, using real NASA data from DONKI, the Astronomy Picture of the Day and the Planetary Fact Sheet. It was built with Python, Flask, Flask-SocketIO, SQLite, JavaScript, Three.js, Web Audio, HTML and CSS, with Claude (Anthropic) assisting on the code, which is labelled throughout. We kept the engineering numbers simplified for gameplay, added fallbacks so the game keeps running if a data service fails, protected passwords and keys, and used no NASA branding or AI-generated media.
